content_voiceover: This table lays out the ASTCT consensus grading for ICANS, the immune effector cell associated neurotoxicity syndrome that fellows will see after CAR T cell therapy or bispecific antibody treatment for lymphoma. Grading runs across five domains. First, the ICE score, that's the immune effector cell encephalopathy score, used for patients twelve and older, where a score of seven to nine is grade one, three to six is grade two, zero to two is grade three, and a score of zero with the patient unarousable and unable to be tested is grade four. Second, level of consciousness, ranging from spontaneous awakening in grade one, down to arousal only with vigorous or repetitive tactile stimuli, or stupor and coma, in grade four. Third, seizures, which only enter the picture at grade three, with any seizure that resolves quickly, and grade four, with life threatening prolonged seizures lasting more than five minutes or repetitive seizures without return to baseline. Fourth, motor findings, which only appear at grade four, as deep focal motor weakness such as hemiparesis or paraparesis. And fifth, signs of raised intracranial pressure or cerebral edema, appearing at grade three as focal edema on imaging, and at grade four as decerebrate or decorticate posturing, sixth nerve palsy, papilledema, Cushing's triad, or diffuse cerebral edema. The overall ICANS grade is set by the most severe domain present.
keypoints: ASTCT ICANS grading uses five domains
ICE score defines grades one through four in adults
Seizures and motor weakness only appear at grade three and four
Overall grade equals the worst affected domain
keypoint_voiceover: Remember, ICANS grading follows five domains: ICE score, consciousness, seizures, motor findings, and intracranial pressure signs. The ICE score anchors grading in patients twelve and older, from seven to nine at grade one down to zero at grade four. Seizures and focal motor weakness only enter at grade three and four. And critically, the overall grade is always set by whichever domain is most severe.
